properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Mountains
properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued August 28 at 9:59AM PDT until August 28 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT THROUGH 3 PM FRIDAY FOR MANY
INTERIOR PORTIONS OF SOUTHWEST CALIFORNIA DUE TO EXTREME HEAT AND
INSTABILITY ALONG WITH LOCALLY GUSTY/ERRATIC WINDS AND LOW
HUMIDITIES...

...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT THROUGH 3 PM TODAY ACROSS ALL OF
SAN LUIS OBISPO COUNTY TO DO POTENTIAL FOR DRY LIGHTNING...

.A hot and unstable air mass combined with locally gusty/erratic
winds and low humidities will bring continue to bring a risk of
large plume dominated fires with rapid spread and extreme fire
behavior. Additionally, tropical moisture streaming across our
area will bring a 10-25 percent chance of thunderstorms to the
region, with a moderate risk for fire starts across San Luis
Obispo County due to dry lightning potential.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Moderate risk for dry lightning with minimal
rain as well as gusty and erratic winds.

* TEMPERATURES...Highs 90 to 100. Deep mixing heights of 10,000 to
15,000 feet today.

* IMPACTS...Moderate risk for fire starts associated with dry
lightning. Additionally, there is a continued risk of large
plume dominated fires with rapid fire spread and extreme fire
behavior.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. Use extreme caution
with anything that can spark a wildfire. Residents near wildland
interfaces should be prepared to evacuate if a wildfire breaks
out. See readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for
information.

SAN LUIS OBISPO COUNTY TO DO POTENTIAL FOR DRY LIGHTNING...

.A hot and unstable air mass combined with locally gusty/erratic
winds and low humidities will bring continue to bring a risk of
large plume dominated fires with rapid spread and extreme fire
behavior. Additionally, tropical moisture streaming across our
area will bring a 10-25 percent chance of thunderstorms to the

humidities in the 15 to 30 percent range.

* IMPACTS...There is a continued risk of large plume dominated
fires with rapid fire spread and extreme fire behavior. There is
a history of large plume dominated fires this time of year with

properties.areaDesc: Yavapai County Valleys and Basins
properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued August 28 at 9:40AM MST until August 28 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions, with temperatures around 105 to
110 expected below 4000 feet.

* WHERE...Yavapai County below 4000 feet; including the Verde Valley
and Black Canyon City.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Most individuals will be at risk for heat-related
illnesses without effective cooling or adequate hydration,
especially with prolonged outdoor exposure.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke.
Anyone overcome by heat should be moved to a cool and shaded
location. Heat stroke is an emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Stay cool, stay hydrated, stay informed.

NWSheadline: EXTREME HEAT WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 8 PM MST THIS EVENING BELOW 4000 FEET

properties.areaDesc: Grand Canyon Country
properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued August 28 at 9:40AM MST until August 28 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions expected below 4000 feet, with
daytime temperatures ranging from 93 to 97 degrees at Havasupai
Gardens, to 106 to 110 degrees at Phantom Ranch.

* WHERE...Lower elevations of the Grand Canyon.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Most individuals will be at risk for heat-related
illnesses without effective cooling or adequate hydration,
especially with prolonged outdoor exposure.
properties.instruction:
This warning is reserved for only the hottest days of the year and is
issued when temperatures are expected to rise to dangerous levels.

Day hikers on Bright Angel Trail should descend no farther than 1 1/2
miles from the upper trailhead. Between the hours of 10 AM and 4 PM,
hikers should be out of the canyon or at Havasupai Gardens or Bright
Angel campgrounds, physical activity is discouraged. All hikers
should have adequate gear, including a wide-brimmed hat, sunscreen,
salty snacks, sufficient water, and electrolyte mix. Doubling your
calorie intake helps maintain your energy.

Hike smart.

Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke.
Anyone overcome by heat should be moved to a cool and shaded
location. Heat stroke is an emergency! Call 9 1 1.

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach out
20 NM...
Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach from 20 to
60 NM...

* Until 100 PM CDT.

* At 1100 AM CDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from 13 nm
southwest of Okaloosa Deep Water Reef to 42 nm southeast of
Oriskany Reef to 67 nm west of Empire Mica Wreck, moving east at 15
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Laguna Beach, Santa Rosa Beach, and Panama City Beach.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued August 28 at 6:51AM PDT until August 28 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 3 PM PDT THIS AFTERNOON
DUE TO LIGHTNING FOR SANTA CRUZ MOUNTAINS, SOUTHERN SALINAS
VALLEY/ARROYO SECO AND LAKE SAN ANTONIO, SANTA LUCIA MOUNTAINS AND
LOS PADRES NATIONAL FOREST, NORTHERN SALINAS VALLEY/HOLLISTER VALLEY
AND CARMEL VALLEY, NORTHERN MONTEREY BAY, AND SOUTHERN MONTEREY BAY
AND BIG SUR COAST...

....The potential for isolated thunderstorms across the Central Coast
continues from this morning through Friday afternoon...

* AFFECTED AREA...The Salinas and Carmel Valleys and Hollister Area,
Monterey Bay and the Big Sur Coast, The Santa Cruz Mountains, and
Interior Monterey County and the Santa Lucia Range.

* TIMING...Until 3 PM PDT this afternoon.

* THUNDERSTORMS...Lightning strikes with little precipitation and
gusty and erratic outflow winds of 40 to 50 mph.

* IMPACTS...There will be an increased risk for power outages.
Lightning strikes may result in new fire ignitions. Erratic outflow
winds will result in rapid fire spread for both new and existing
fires.
properties.instruction:
Please advise responding agencies or fire crews in the field of this
fire weather alert.

Never leave burning debris or camp fires unattended; extinguish them
completely. Avoid using equipment or machinery that could create a
spark. Secure tow chains to avoid dragging and subsequent sparks.
Never toss cigarette butts out of your vehicle's window. Remember,
one less spark, one less flame.

Familiarize yourself with your emergency plan! Where will you go? How
will you get there? Do you have your go kit ready to go? Who will you
call to let others know you are safe? Visit ready.gov/plan for more
information.

properties.description:

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during

properties.instruction:
To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.
